items.statement: Cash of Rs 60-65 crore held as collateral for non-fund-based limits to issue bank guarantees and SBLCs for gas volumes
items.quote: On 30th September we had cash of around 60 crores, 60, 65 crores, I think.

items.statement: Capital is used as collateral for non-fund-based limits to provide bank guarantees and SBLCs for securing gas volumes
items.quote: The capital is being used for getting us. Non-fund-based limits. The money is there in the account as collateral. We are taking guarantees based on that, and providing the Bgs and Sblc for securing the volumes that we are picking up.

items.statement: GSK China will sell technology and 9 IPRs to IMPCO Mexico for USD 5.1 million (~₹43.5 crore) at arm's length price.
items.quote: Second outcome is to sell the technology know -how and nine IPRs by GSK China to IMPCO Mexico for about USD 5.1 million i.e. close to ₹ 43 crores.

items.statement: GSK China will use net proceeds (~₹40 crore) to repay loan to Symphony India, reducing outstanding from ₹49.6 crore to ~₹10 crore.
items.value: ₹40 crores net proceeds; outstanding loan ~₹10 crores
items.quote: So, net of taxes and expenses , close to ₹40 crores, GSK , China will use to repay the loan to Symphony, India. Loan outstanding from GSK, China to Symphony, India was about ₹60 crores as on 1st April 2024. Over the last 12 months, close to ₹13.5 crores have been repaid and as of today, including interest accrued, the outstanding is ₹49.6 crores. So, post completion of this transaction, the outsta

items.statement: Symphony India holds a treasury of ~₹600 crores currently.
items.quote: Because you appreciate that the process has begun. We have some feelers, we have some indications , but once it is fully wrapped up, we will come to know the precise number and details. So just as a cautionary statement. This is anyway going to impact, the reason being, finally, apart from this currently, Symphony, India is sitting on a treasury of ~ ₹600 crores.

items.statement: Symphony India has zero related party transactions other than normal course sales/purchases with subsidiaries and managerial remuneration.
items.quote: As many of you may be aware, it has been the practice of Symphony that other than sales and purchase transactions between Symphony and subsidiary or inter se amongst subsidiaries as well as managerial remuneration, both of which are absolutely in normal course of business, there are zero related party transactions.

items.statement: CEO Ram Praveen steps down; Hemant Sikka appointed as new CEO by MLL Board
items.quote: The Mahindra Logistics Board has accepted his resignation and the Mahindra Logistics Board has also appointed Hemant Sikka as the CEO of the company.

items.statement: Total cash and cash equivalents grew to INR 622 crores from INR 473 crores at end of last year.
items.quote: The total cash and cash equivalent that we had in the company has now grown to INR 622 crores as compared to INR 473 crores that we had at the end of last year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow grew more than 30% year-on-year and DSOs improved to 83 days.
items.quote: And if you look at this year also, we've generated more than 30% growth in cash year -on-year. So we feel comfortable with the working capital situation that we have and our DSOs are also consistently improving.

items.statement: Debtors increased as of 31st March 2025 due to revenue skew towards last four months and longer collection cycles in opportunity states.
items.quote: As a result, as of 31st March 2025, the debtors were higher versus the previous years.

items.statement: Preferential allotment is underway and expected to close shortly.
items.quote: Yes, yes, that is under way as of now and we would be closing this shortly.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to PAT was 98.8% and free cash flow to PAT was 78.5% for FY25
items.quote: Cash generation for the year continued to drive the strength of our balance sheet, with operating cash flow to PAT at 98.8% and free cash flow to PAT at 78.5% for the full year.

items.statement: Cash and investment balance reached an all-time high of US$1.56 billion or INR 13,346 crores as of March 31, 2025
items.quote: We closed the year with an all-time high Cash and Investment balance of US$1.56 billion or INR 13,346 crores compared to INR 12,488 crores in Q3 FY'25.

items.statement: Total DSO improved by 1 day to 79 days in Q4 versus Q3
items.quote: We remain committed to reducing our day's sales outstanding as evidenced by the improvement in total DSO, which reduced by 1 day, bringing it to 79 days for Q4 versus Q3.

items.statement: Net debt is INR 435 crores as of year-end, flat versus previous quarter; management targets INR 100-120 crore reduction in current year as capex cycle pauses.
items.quote: Our net debt is about INR 435 crores as of the year-end. And if I remember correctly, the quarter before, I think it was somewhere around INR 300 crores and something.

items.statement: Management expects at least INR 100-120 crore net debt reduction in FY26 despite planned capex of INR 50-60 crore for machining and INR 15-20 crore for lamination.
items.quote: Despite that, I think you should look at INR 100 crore to INR 120 crore reduction in net debt at the barest minimum.

items.statement: Chennai plant loss of INR11-12 crore hit bottom line; INR10 crore trial run losses capitalized per IND-AS
items.quote: We made a loss of around INR11 crores, INR12 crores in Chennai, which has hit the bottom line by around INR11 crores. And I think INR10 crores we have capitalized as trial run losses, we could do that as per the IND-AS accounting standard.

items.statement: Cash and liquid fund balance of Rs 439 crore as of 31 March 2025
items.quote: As of 31st March '25, we are pleased to report a healthy cash and liquid fund balance of 439 crore and will further work to improve capital efficiency.

items.statement: New plant to be financed through equity and debt mix; Aichi may increase stake, promoters may invest, QIP possible for any gap
items.quote: funding is, as I said, equity, we have said in the past also, our partners at some sta ge will increase their stake. Now when do they increase their stake, that is up to them. So, in th e next 3 years, at some stage, they will increase their stake, and so that will be one source of funding. And at some stage, if they invest, the promoter might also like to pitch in a bit. An d then if there is a g

items.statement: Company plans to raise INR500-750 crores fresh capital after shareholder approval on March 2nd; format (QIP, preferential, rights) still under evaluation.
items.quote: Apart from that, we continue with our plans on the equity raise. We are on track, we got the shareholder approval on the 2nd of March and once we come up with the results, we will be on course to raising the INR500 crores to INR750 crores of fresh capital that we had planned.

items.statement: Promoters hold 35% plus 5% management; no further dilution planned and promoter warrants to be subscribed before September will increase holding
items.quote: No, so there are no plans of further dilution. There are. The numbers will only at all points in that. These numbers will remain constant, or they'll go up from here.

items.statement: Promoters will subscribe to share warrants before September increasing their holding
items.quote: Also, one more point Raja. The there are the share warrants which the promoters are going to subscribe. So by, you know, before September, so that is also which will increase the promoters holding.

items.statement: DSO improved over last year despite heavy deal signing in second half; 90% of receivables are less than 180 days
items.quote: Our days is outstanding. We've improved over last year now, despite this year, being a heavy year in terms of. In the second half of the year. We have signed a lot of deals, but our DSO has still improved over the last year, and one more important point here.

items.statement: 90% of receivables are less than 180 days
items.quote: are 90% of our receivables are less than 180 days right payal?

items.statement: Equity-cum-debt raise of USD 13 million nearly complete; equity money received, debt signing in progress to close within 30 days
items.quote: The current raise we are, we are finished. We are doing an equity. Come debt deal. So we are just signing papers right now. So a lot of the equity money has come in the debt. Signing is happening as we speak. so we should complete all of these over the next 30 days.

items.statement: ESOP expense is 3.3 crores out of total employee cost
items.quote: out of the total employee cost the ESOP expenses is 3.3 crores.

items.statement: Positive cash flow from operations was 5.62 Cr for FY25.
items.quote: positive cash flow from operations stand at 5.62 Cr.

items.statement: Receivable days increased due to 40-50% of business occurring in last quarter and 40-50% of receivables are against creditors for joint projects
items.quote: The number of day has increased , because as I earlier also mentioned that 40% to 50% delay happened in the last quarter. So it's always a pressure on the government also to conclude before the financial year end because they have to use the funds.

items.statement: Board approved QIP of INR7,500 crore and long-term bonds of INR10,000 crore; timing and mode to be decided after shareholder and government approvals
items.quote: We have moved this paper, but there is a process which will follow after this. We have to go to shareholders, AGM and then government and get the approval.

items.statement: Cyber-attack on IT infrastructure notified to exchanges on April 10, 2025; systems isolated, critical apps restored next working day, minimal business impact, data safe
items.quote: I would also like to address a recent cyber -attack on our IT infrastructure, which we notified to the exchanges on April 10, 2025.

items.statement: Board approved grant of 4,16,972 stock units under PSU 2023 at INR 10 per unit and 17,23,149 stock options under ESOP 2023 at INR 577.79 per option
items.quote: Grant of 4,16,972 stock units under the ‘Nippon Life India Asset Management Limited –Performance linked Stock Unit Scheme 2023’ (“PSU 2023”) at INR 10.00 per stock unit. o Grant of 17,23,149 stock options under the ‘Nippon Life India Asset Management Limited – Employee Stock Option Scheme 2023’ (“ESOP 2023”) at INR 577.79 per stock option

items.statement: Receivables grew around 10% to INR55,840 crores in March quarter versus INR50,846 crores in March '24 quarter
items.quote: Receivables have grown by around 10% to reach INR55,840 crores in March quarter versus INR50,846 crores in March '24 quarter.

items.statement: Advances from customers are around INR4,300-4,400 crores as per contract liabilities on balance sheet
items.quote: So currently roughly about I can say around INR4,300 crores or INR4,400 crores is what we have as advances.

items.statement: Debtor days increased from 81 to 101 days due to rapid business growth, causing negative operating cash flow despite profit growth
items.quote: See, if you have seen last quarter, our debtor days was 81 days and which has increased to 101 days. Everything, all receivable, all profit is converting into cash. Since the business has drastically gone up, the number of the debtor days has increased.

items.statement: Debtor days at 101 days, expected to reduce to 80-90 days over next 2-3 quarters as billing cycles stabilize
items.quote: Yes. See, but since we are working with government business, it will be anywhere between 80 to 90 days for some period of time. Once the cycles get established, it will reduce. So I see another 2 quarters to 3 quarters, it will be between 80 to 90 days.

items.statement: Increase in current and non-current assets of INR 269 crores driven by vendor advances for Q1 execution and unbilled revenue from Feb-March business
items.quote: This is more of a vendor advance and another is the unbilled revenue. One is the vendor advance for the business for the first quarter, which we have already booked and will be executing in the April month, majorly in the April month and the May month.

items.statement: Preferential equity infusion of INR 905 crores, INR 512 crores received so far, remaining to fund EV fleet expansion to 5,000 by FY27
items.quote: Sir, out of INR 905 crores rate, INR 512 crores we have received. Whatever the borrowings are there, that is only the LC, sir. And whereas if you see the bank balance, which is there, plus there is a vehicle loan because of that, that vehicle loan which is payable within less than 12 months being classified under the short-term borrowing.

items.statement: EV fleet expansion to 5,000 by FY27 funded 80% by vehicle loans, equity requirement of INR 50-60 crores covered by preferential issue proceeds
items.quote: So most of these vehicles, we're going to raise a vehicle loan of about 80%. And the equity requirement is not going to be very high, it will be roughly about INR 50 crores, INR 60 crores. I think we already have raised enough capital. And there's more money, which is going to come from the preferential issue.

items.statement: GST demand of INR 29 crores under Section 74 treated as contingent liability, no provision made, confident of winning appeal
items.quote: Only it has been classified as a contingent liability. There is no provisions required. We are confident that we'll win this case in the appeal.

items.statement: Receivables have decreased significantly as funds are being received; over 50% of March 31 receivables already collected
items.quote: So I believe I stated before, like this data is as on 31st March. So whatever receivables were there, we have started receiving the receivables. And significantly of that, like you can say 50% or above has already been received.
